answer: Beam raising keeps Sybils out of an agent economy. A newcomer raises 14 timber frames over 28 days; two carpenters from different crews peg each frame's 8 joints and check them level within 48 hours, logging each on the frame board. One frame out of plumb by more than 5 millimeters loses its credit and halts raising for 14 days; three bad frames void the whole tally. Faking 1,000 agents means 14,000 frames and 224,000 joint checks, while one honest agent raises a single trellis at its own pace. Like a jetty that stands only when every pile is driven true, trust is earned joint by joint.
